outcome: survival to discharge without severe neonatal morbidity (bronchopulmonary dysplasia, grade 3 or grade 4 intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular leukomalacia, stage 2 or stage 3 necrotizing enterocolitis)
cohort: 424 diamniotic twin pregnancies between 26 0/7 and 31 6/7 weeks of gestation
finding: Planned cesarean delivery for very preterm twins was not associated with higher survival to discharge without severe neonatal morbidity compared to planned vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The study found that planned mode of delivery (cesarean or vaginal) was not associated with survival to discharge without severe neonatal morbidity in very preterm twins.
